title: Titanium Ion Implantation Electrode
function: Ion extraction electrode disk for implanter
alloyReason: Grade 5 Ti-6Al-4V (UNS R56400) is specified for Titanium Ion Implantation Electrode because its non-magnetic permeability (µ <1.0001) eliminates interference with electron beam trajectories in vacuum processing chambers. The low sputter yield of Ti (0.3 atoms/ion at 500eV Ar+) compared to Al (1.2) reduces cross-contamination in thin-film deposition tools. Matched thermal expansion (8.6 µm/m°C) with ceramic end-effectors prevents particle generation during thermal cycling — critical for Ion extraction electrode disk for implanter. This rationale is driven by ion extraction electrode disk for implanter and service environment demands.
process: Cleanroom CNC Class 100 for ion implant geometry
UHP DI water cascade rinse with SPC sampling
Particle count MIL-STD-1246 with SPC sampling
surfaceTreatment: Electropolishing Ra <0.25um + UHP DI cascade rinse with particle count verification per MIL-STD-1246 Class 1 — tailored for ion extraction electrode application
commonFailures: Outgassing H2O CH4 >1% AMU 100 - mitigated by 200C vacuum bake-out 24h to desorb trapped species — critical for ion extraction electrode performance

faq.q: Is Titanium Ion Implantation Electrode compatible with fluorine-based process chemistries?
faq.a: Grade 5 Ti-6Al-4V has excellent resistance to NF₃, CF₄, SF₆, and other fluorine-based plasma chemistries used in semiconductor etching and chamber cleaning. The TiO₂ passive layer forms a stable TiF₄ reaction product that does not spall or generate particles. However, Titanium Ion Implantation Electrode should not be used in HF-containing wet processes where corrosion rates exceed 0.5 mm/year.

faq.q: What material certifications are provided with Titanium Ion Implantation Electrode?

Dimensional inspection reports and Certificate of Conformance (CoC) are standard. First Article Inspection Reports (FAIR) per AS9102 are available on request for ion extraction electrode.
